title: Perception and Acceptability of Reusing Treated Wastewater: Determining Factors and Public Engagement Strategies
content:
ABSTRACT

The treatment and reuse of wastewater are vital tools for managing water resources, with public acceptability being crucial for their success. This study reviews public perceptions and acceptance of treated wastewater reuse, identifying key factors and engagement strategies. A systematic review of selected articles from databases was conducted, using the KH Coder software for text mining and network analysis to uncover themes and connections. Results indicate substantial public support, particularly for indirect reuse, but beliefs and a lack of awareness significantly impact acceptance. Effective engagement strategies must include safety assurances, educational campaigns, economic incentives, and public participation. Clear communication, specific regulations, and segregated water networks are essential for the successful adoption of treated wastewater reuse.
